image_description: A male mallard duck (drake) standing on a grassy bank near water. The duck features the characteristic iridescent green head, white neck ring, chestnut breast, and grey/brown body plumage. It has a yellow bill and orange webbed feet. The background consists of blurred dry branches and water.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The bill is clearly visible, broad, and flat with a distinct yellow coloration typical of a male mallard.
The eye is visible against the dark green head feathers and appears dark/black.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is stocky and compact, streamlined and buoyant with dense waterproof plumage.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The body shape is consistent with a duck, appearing compact and covered in smooth, dense-looking feathers.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Breeding plumage is typically more colorful than female: common patterns include iridescent green head with white neck ring and grey body (mallard), or chestnut head with grey body.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image displays the classic male mallard pattern: iridescent green head, distinct white neck ring, chestnut breast, and greyish-brown flanks.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Legs are short and set far back on the body with webbed feet (three forward toes connected by webbing).
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The orange legs are visible. The feet show clear webbing between the toes, consistent with aquatic bird anatomy.
The folded wing is visible on the side of the body, showing proper feather layering and structure.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Tail is short with curled central tail feathers (drake feathers) in many species.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The tail is short, and the characteristic upward curl of the central tail feathers (drake feathers) is clearly visible at the rear.
